questions.stem: A pharmacology student compares five experimental inhaled anesthetics. Agent A: blood/gas partition coefficient 0.65, minimum alveolar concentration (MAC) 2.0%. Agent B: blood/gas 2.4, MAC 0.75%. Agent C: blood/gas 0.42, MAC 6.0%. Agent D: blood/gas 12, MAC 0.2%. Agent E: blood/gas 1.4, MAC 1.2%. All other conditions are the same. Which agent will most likely produce the fastest induction of anesthesia?
choices: Agent A
Agent B
Agent C
Agent D
Agent E
questions.explanation: Speed of induction depends on **solubility in blood**. A gas with a **low blood/gas partition coefficient** (Agent C, 0.42) dissolves poorly in blood, so its partial pressure in blood and brain rises quickly. Agent D is the most **potent** (lowest MAC), but it is very soluble in blood, so it has the **slowest** induction and recovery. Potency and speed of onset are separate properties.
questions.explanation_pt: A velocidade de indução depende da **solubilidade no sangue**. Um gás com **baixo coeficiente de partição sangue/gás** (Agente C, 0,42) se dissolve pouco no sangue, e sua pressão parcial no sangue e no cérebro sobe rápido. O Agente D é o mais **potente** (menor CAM), mas é muito solúvel no sangue, por isso tem a indução e a recuperação **mais lentas**. Potência e rapidez de início são propriedades diferentes.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man became paraplegic after a spinal cord injury 5 weeks ago. He now needs urgent surgery for a bowel obstruction, and succinylcholine is given for rapid intubation. Two minutes later, the ECG shows peaked T waves and a wide QRS complex, and he develops ventricular fibrillation. Serum potassium was 4.2 mEq/L before surgery and is now 7.9 mEq/L. Temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), end-tidal CO2 is normal, and there is no muscle rigidity. Which mechanism best explains the rise in potassium?
choices: Uncontrolled calcium release through a mutant ryanodine receptor
Inhibition of the Na+/K+-ATPase in skeletal muscle
Potassium shift out of cells caused by severe metabolic acidosis
Low aldosterone with reduced renal potassium excretion
Extrajunctional nicotinic receptors after loss of nerve input
questions.explanation: After **denervation** (including spinal cord injury or stroke), burns or crush injury, muscle makes many **extrajunctional nicotinic receptors** across its whole surface. **Succinylcholine** depolarizes all of them at once, and a large amount of potassium leaves the muscle within minutes, causing **hyperkalemic arrest**. Malignant hyperthermia (mutant **ryanodine receptor**) can also raise potassium, but it comes with rigidity, rising end-tidal CO2 and fever, which are absent here.
questions.explanation_pt: Após **desnervação** (inclusive lesão medular ou AVC), queimaduras ou lesão por esmagamento, o músculo produz muitos **receptores nicotínicos extrajuncionais** em toda a sua superfície. A **succinilcolina** despolariza todos ao mesmo tempo, e grande quantidade de potássio sai do músculo em minutos, causando **parada cardíaca por hipercalemia**. A hipertermia maligna (**receptor de rianodina** mutante) também pode elevar o potássio, mas vem com rigidez, aumento do CO2 expirado (capnografia) e febre, ausentes aqui.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman needs a small skin lesion removed from her forearm under local anesthesia. Two years ago she developed hives, lip swelling and wheezing a few minutes after a nerve block with procaine. Allergy testing at that time showed sensitivity to para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA). Which local anesthetic is the most appropriate choice for her procedure?
choices: Tetracaine
Chloroprocaine
Benzocaine
Lidocaine
Cocaine
questions.explanation: Procaine is an **ester** local anesthetic. Esters are broken down by plasma cholinesterase to **PABA**, which causes most true local anesthetic allergies, so **all esters** should be avoided. **Lidocaine** is an **amide**, is metabolized by the liver and does not form PABA. Benzocaine may seem safe because it is only used on the skin, but it is also an ester.
questions.explanation_pt: A procaína é um anestésico local do tipo **éster**. Os ésteres são degradados pela colinesterase plasmática em **PABA**, responsável pela maioria das alergias verdadeiras a anestésicos locais, então **todos os ésteres** devem ser evitados. A **lidocaína** é uma **amida**, é metabolizada pelo fígado e não forma PABA. A benzocaína pode parecer segura por ser só de uso tópico, mas também é um éster.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old man with generalized epilepsy has taken valproate for 3 years. Because seizures continue, lamotrigine is added, and his dose is increased on the schedule normally used for patients who take no other antiepileptic drugs. Four weeks later he has fever, a painful red rash with dark target-like lesions and blisters, and erosions on the lips and inside the mouth. Which mechanism most likely increased his risk of this reaction?
choices: Valproate inhibits glucuronidation of lamotrigine, raising its level
Valproate induces hepatic CYP3A4, producing a toxic lamotrigine metabolite
Lamotrigine inhibits valproate metabolism, raising the valproate level
Lamotrigine displaces valproate from albumin, raising free valproate
Valproate reduces renal clearance of lamotrigine by blocking tubular secretion
questions.explanation: This is **Stevens-Johnson syndrome**, the most feared reaction to **lamotrigine**; risk rises with **high levels** and **fast dose increases**. **Valproate inhibits** the liver enzymes that **glucuronidate** lamotrigine, so lamotrigine levels roughly double and the dose must be raised much more slowly. Valproate is an enzyme **inhibitor**, not an inducer, so a CYP3A4 induction mechanism does not fit.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se da **síndrome de Stevens-Johnson**, a reação mais temida da **lamotrigina**; o risco aumenta com **níveis altos** e **aumento rápido da dose**. O **valproato inibe** as enzimas hepáticas que fazem a **glicuronidação** da lamotrigina, então os níveis de lamotrigina aproximadamente dobram e a dose deve ser aumentada bem mais devagar. O valproato é um **inibidor** enzimático, não um indutor, então um mecanismo de indução do CYP3A4 não se aplica.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman started a drug 8 months ago to prevent frequent migraines. Since then she has lost 6 kg and has trouble finding words. Today she has severe right flank pain that spreads to the groin, and urinalysis shows blood. Serum studies: sodium 139 mEq/L, chloride 113 mEq/L, bicarbonate 17 mEq/L, potassium 3.4 mEq/L. Urine pH is 6.8. CT shows a small stone in the right ureter. Which drug action best explains her stone?
choices: Blockade of T-type calcium channels in thalamic neurons
Inhibition of carbonic anhydrase in the renal tubule
Agonism at serotonin 5-HT1B/1D receptors
Blockade of beta-1 and beta-2 adrenergic receptors
Binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels
questions.explanation: Weight loss, word-finding trouble and kidney stones in a patient taking a migraine preventive point to **topiramate**. It **inhibits carbonic anhydrase**, causing a **normal anion gap metabolic acidosis** (anion gap 139 - 113 - 17 = 9), alkaline urine and low urinary citrate, which favor **calcium phosphate stones**. Propranolol is also a migraine preventive, but it does not cause acidosis or stones; it more often causes fatigue and weight gain.
questions.explanation_pt: Perda de peso, dificuldade para encontrar palavras e cálculo renal em paciente que usa preventivo de enxaqueca apontam para o **topiramato**. Ele **inibe a anidrase carbônica**, causando **acidose metabólica com ânion gap normal** (ânion gap 139 - 113 - 17 = 9), urina alcalina e citrato urinário baixo, o que favorece **cálculos de fosfato de cálcio**. O propranolol também é preventivo de enxaqueca, mas não causa acidose nem cálculos; causa mais fadiga e ganho de peso.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man who has injected heroin several times a day for 2 years wants treatment for opioid use disorder. His last injection was 3 hours ago, and he is calm, with small pupils. He is given sublingual buprenorphine. Thirty minutes later he is restless and yawning, with dilated pupils, a runny nose, goosebumps, abdominal cramps and diarrhea. Which property of buprenorphine best explains these new symptoms?
choices: It is a full mu agonist with a very short half-life
It is a mu antagonist with no agonist activity
It binds mu receptors tightly but activates them only partly
It stimulates kappa receptors and causes dysphoria and restlessness
It induces CYP3A4 and speeds up heroin clearance
questions.explanation: Buprenorphine is a **partial mu agonist** with **very high receptor affinity**. Given while heroin still occupies the receptors, it pushes heroin off and replaces full activation with weaker activation, so the patient goes into **precipitated withdrawal**. For this reason it is started only after early withdrawal signs appear. It is not a pure antagonist like naloxone; its partial agonist effect is why it can treat opioid use disorder.
questions.explanation_pt: A buprenorfina é um **agonista parcial mu** com **afinidade muito alta** pelo receptor. Dada enquanto a heroína ainda ocupa os receptores, ela desloca a heroína e troca a ativação plena por uma ativação mais fraca, e o paciente entra em **abstinência precipitada**. Por isso só é iniciada depois que surgem os primeiros sinais de abstinência. Não é um antagonista puro como a naloxona; seu efeito de agonista parcial é o motivo de servir para tratar o transtorno por uso de opioides.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man with Parkinson disease has taken carbidopa-levodopa for 3 years. Six months ago ropinirole was added. His wife now reports that he has spent most of their savings on online gambling and has started compulsive late-night shopping. He had no such behavior before. Which action of the added drug best explains this change?
choices: D2/D3 receptor stimulation in the mesolimbic pathway
Inhibition of peripheral DOPA decarboxylase
Inhibition of catechol-O-methyltransferase
Blockade of muscarinic receptors in the striatum
Blockade of NMDA glutamate receptors in the basal ganglia
questions.explanation: Ropinirole and pramipexole are **non-ergot dopamine agonists**. They act directly on **D2** and especially **D3** receptors, which are dense in the **mesolimbic reward pathway**, so they can cause **impulse control disorders** such as gambling, shopping, binge eating and hypersexuality; they also cause sudden **sleep attacks**. Peripheral DOPA decarboxylase inhibition is the action of carbidopa, which he took for years without this problem.
questions.explanation_pt: O ropinirol e o pramipexol são **agonistas dopaminérgicos não ergóticos**. Eles agem diretamente nos receptores **D2** e sobretudo **D3**, abundantes na **via mesolímbica de recompensa**, e por isso podem causar **transtornos do controle de impulsos**, como jogo patológico, compras compulsivas, compulsão alimentar e hipersexualidade; também causam **ataques de sono** súbitos. A inibição da DOPA descarboxilase periférica é a ação da carbidopa, que ele usou por anos sem esse problema.

questions.stem: A 79-year-old woman with Alzheimer disease fainted at home while standing up from a chair. She has taken amlodipine for hypertension for 6 years. Donepezil was started 6 weeks ago. Vital signs now: pulse 42/min and regular, blood pressure 96/58 mm Hg, respirations 14/min. ECG shows sinus bradycardia with a normal PR interval. She also reports nausea and loose stools since starting her newest drug. Which mechanism best explains her bradycardia?
choices: Blockade of NMDA receptors in the brainstem
Blockade of L-type calcium channels in the AV node
Blockade of beta-1 adrenergic receptors in the SA node
More acetylcholine acting on cardiac M2 receptors
Reduced thyroid hormone production
questions.explanation: **Donepezil** inhibits **acetylcholinesterase** in the body as well as in the brain. More acetylcholine reaches **M2 receptors** in the SA and AV nodes, so the heart rate slows, which can cause **syncope**; the same cholinergic excess explains her nausea and diarrhea. **Amlodipine** is a dihydropyridine that acts mainly on vascular smooth muscle, has little effect on the nodes, and she took it for years without trouble.
questions.explanation_pt: A **donepezila** inibe a **acetilcolinesterase** no corpo e também no cérebro. Mais acetilcolina chega aos **receptores M2** dos nós sinusal e atrioventricular, e a frequência cardíaca cai, o que pode causar **síncope**; o mesmo excesso colinérgico explica a náusea e a diarreia. O **anlodipino** é uma di-hidropiridina que age sobretudo no músculo liso vascular, tem pouco efeito sobre os nós, e ela o usou por anos sem problema.
